samples.summary: Single-use `/start` is at odds with the documented headless copy-paste path it is supposed to preserve
samples.evidence: cli.md:176-178 now says step 3 "Opens (and prints, for copy-paste in headless environments) the nonce-free http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start", and cli.md:206-211 claims "the URL a headless user copies is the same one `open()` is given and the same one that works". Those two properties cannot both hold with a one-shot route: `login` always calls `open(startUrl)` (packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:72) and only falls into the `catch` when the dynamic import or spawn itself throws — `open()` resolves normally in headless/CI environments where a launcher binary exists (xdg-open, `start`, wslview) but no browser ever renders, and browsers can also issue more than one request to a URL (prefetch/preconnect, restored tab). In those cases the first `GET /start` consumes the nonce and the URL the CLI just told the user to visit ("If the browser does not open, visit the URL above.", login.ts:68) answers `410 START_CONSUMED_MESSAGE`, leaving the invocation with no way to complete — a regression against the prior behaviour, which printed a URL that still worked when the browser did not appear. The design doc asserts the property rather than reconciling it (e.g. allowing re-issue until the callback arrives, or only arming single-use after a successful open).

samples.summary: The printed hand-off URL no longer shows which server the login targets
samples.evidence: `console.error(`Opening browser: ${startUrl}`)` now prints only `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start`. cli.md §3 documents `--server` / `WAFFLEBASE_SERVER` / self-hosting as first-class, and the previous line printed `${server}/auth/github?mode=cli&port=…`, which let the user confirm the target deployment before consenting. Suppressing the nonce did not require suppressing the origin; printing the server alongside the loopback URL would keep both properties.

samples.summary: `warn` option on `startCallbackServer` exists only for tests, widening the production API surface
samples.evidence: `options: { allowUnbound?: boolean; warn?: (message: string) => void }` — the only caller in `src` (login.ts:48-50) never passes `warn`; it is supplied only by packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts. A test-only seam in the exported signature is a small design smell; capturing `console.error` in the test, or documenting the seam as such, keeps the public shape aligned with real usage.

samples.summary: Legitimate version skew now costs a 30-second wall-clock wait for the actionable message
samples.evidence: The doc previously promised the nonce-less callback "fails the login immediately with an actionable message instead of the 30-second timeout"; it now reads "The version-skew message replaces the timeout message when the 30 seconds expire" (cli.md:225-227, mirrored at login.ts:373-385). The security rationale for not aborting is stated, but the honest cost — every user of an older self-hosted server waits the full timeout before being told to upgrade or pass `--allow-unbound-callback` — is a UX trade-off the doc presents as free. A shorter dedicated deadline once a nonce-less callback has been seen would keep both properties; at minimum the doc should own the wait.

verdict.reason: All quoted evidence checks out in the working tree. docs/design/cli.md:175-177 documents step 3 as opening AND printing the one-shot http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start for headless copy-paste, and cli.md:209-211 asserts "the URL a headless user copies is the same one `open()` is given and the same one that works" while stating a second GET /start returns 410. packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:266-281 implements exactly that: `startConsumed` is latched on the first request with no re-arm, no re-issue until the callback arrives, and no deferral of single-use until a successful browser render; packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts:212-219 pins the 302-then-410 behaviour. login.ts:67-75 prints the same URL with "If the browser does not open, visit the URL above." and only reports failure when the dynamic import/spawn throws, so a launcher that spawns without rendering (or a prefetch/restored tab) can consume the URL the user was just told to visit. The doc also still advertises the copy-paste fallback in its risk table (cli.md:1187) without reconciling it against the one-shot route. No guard elsewhere makes this unreachable: the only check on /start is the authorizeUrl===null 503 arming check (login.ts:267-271). Non-Goal cli.md:59 ("Device flow or headless authentication") could be read as narrowing the obligation, but the doc affirmatively claims the copy-paste property in the same section, so the inconsistency is internal to the spec and needs the author to resolve it. Not refutable on not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope grounds.

finding.summary: Headless copy-paste login is broken while the design doc still promises it. `docs/design/cli.md:176` (unchanged by this diff) still says step 3 "also prints URL for copy-paste in headless environments", but the happy path now prints `.../auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>` WITHOUT `cliState`, and the removed line "If the browser does not open, visit the URL above." is only replaced inside the `catch` of `open()`. On a headless box where `open()` resolves without actually launching a browser (a very common case — `open` shells out to xdg-open/`$BROWSER` and frequently succeeds nominally), the only URL the user can copy is the nonce-less one. Following it makes the backend start a flow with `cliState: undefined`, redirect without `state`, and the listener then rejects with UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE telling the user to upgrade the server or pass `--allow-unbound-callback` — advice that is false for an up-to-date server and pushes them to disable the very binding this change adds. Either keep printing the full URL (the doc's contract) or update cli.md step 3 and the headless story to match.
finding.evidence: login.ts:71-87 builds `oauthUrl` with cliState but prints the stripped form unconditionally; full URL printed only in the `catch`. docs/design/cli.md:176 still claims the URL is printed for copy-paste in headless environments.

verdict.reason: The finding's evidence is not present in the working tree. login.ts prints `startUrl` (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start`, built at L399), never the stripped `.../auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>`; grep for `oauthUrl` across the repo returns no source hits. The line 'If the browser does not open, visit the URL above.' is printed unconditionally at L68 *before* the try/catch — the catch at L73-75 prints a different message ('Could not open a browser automatically.'). The `/start` route (L266-281) 302s once to buildAuthorizeUrl(...) which does include `&cliState=` (L209-212), so the URL a headless user copies is the one that works and the claimed nonce-less flow / UNBOUND_CALLBACK_MESSAGE downgrade path is unreachable from the printed URL. The design doc also already describes this exact behavior: cli.md:175-177 says it opens and prints 'the nonce-free http://127.0.0.1:<port>/start, which 302s the browser, once, to GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<port>&cliState=<nonce>', and cli.md:210-211 states 'the URL a headless user copies is the same one open() is given and the same one that works'. Doc and code agree, so there is no spec/design-doc mismatch under this lens.
